newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hitachi says to boost mobile telecoms business.
newsitem.headline: Hitachi says to boost mobile telecoms business.

text.p: Hitachi Ltd plans to strengthen its mobile telecommunications business, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.
However, the spokesman said he could not comment on the scale of the investment, put in one newspaper report at 40 billion yen.
"The company plans to strengthen its business in that area, but we can not confirm the amount of investment," the spokesman said.
The report was in the Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun.
The newspaper report said Hitachi plans to invest mainly in production facilities for making cellular phones under the Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) standard.
CDMA is a technology for digital transmission of data by cellular phone.

In December 1996, Hitachi and QUALCOMM Inc of the United States signed a multi-million-dollar, royalty-bearing licence agreement for wireless infrastructure equipment based on QUALCOMM's CDMA IS-95 technology.
Under the agreement, Hitachi was granted rights to manufacture and sell CDMA wireless infrastructure worldwide.
